notes: Phase 0 reproduction of the v0.2.0 protocol (1 warm-up + 8 serial runs/lane, receipt verified + journal asserted each run, CPU lane via R0_DISABLE_METAL=1). Reproduced speedups (1.571x/1.734x/1.766x for hello/hash/busy) vs the published v0.2.0 medians (1.70x/1.63x/1.70x): hash and busy came in slightly higher, hello lower (the ~1s single-segment proof is the most variance-sensitive; its CPU lane ran faster this session). All within run-to-run variance on a shared machine; the structural story (eval_check CPU floor bounds the speedup) is unchanged. The hello/hash/busy rows come from the validate.sh bundle evidence/20260614T211748Z (top-level pointer); the multiseg/mempress/shaheavy/ecdsa adopter rows are from evidence/adopter-20260615T102417Z (summary.json sha256 ec7ff1f8ab3759a36e123afedfdaed8552050d9092c35cd976382c9faec87f08), 1 warm-up + 5 serial runs/lane (fewer than 8 because each run is 2-4 min; metal variance was ~0.2%). Each workload's exact files are pinned in its own per-workload evidence block. All four adopter rows cluster at 1.722x-1.732x; their measured circuit floor is ~87% (eval_check ~83%) with ~13% generic-on-GPU, i.e. the speedup holds across ECDSA-verify, SHA-256-heavy, memory-pressure, and long multi-segment proofs and does not erode toward 1x at these sizes.
